title: Importing Crossnacreevy weather data
text: `ImportWeather()` reads Excel workbook containing one worksheet per calendar year. Worksheets must named four-digit year, `2022`, `2023` `2024`. Crossnacreevy workbook layout uses two header rows followed daily observations. importer expects date day--year fields weather columns minimum/maximum temperature, mean air temperature, temperature difference, rainfall, soil temperature 15 cm 45 cm, average wind speed, relative humidity, leaf wetness daily light totals. Keep source workbook unchanged retain copy station’s measurement metadata. data dictionary lists variable labels units exposed package.

title: Monthly summaries and climate normals
text: package provides two monthly summary functions. answer different questions used interchangeably. `MonthlySummaryTable()`: monthly statistics individual year? `ClimateSummaryTable()`: average monthly climatology across years? functions expect long-format data returned `ImportWeather()`.

title: Monthly summaries and climate normals
text: ```{r, eval = FALSE} weather <- ImportWeather( “data/crossnacreevy.xlsx”, start_date = “2018-01-01”, end_date = “2024-12-31” ) monthly_by_year <- MonthlySummaryTable(weather) monthly_by_year ``` result contains one row per year weather variable, calendar months columns. January 2020 January 2021 remain separate rows.

title: Monthly summaries and climate normals
text: ```{r, eval = FALSE} climate_normals <- ClimateSummaryTable(weather) climate_normals ``` climatology function first calculates year’s monthly statistic, takes mean yearly values calendar month variable. rainfall, example, averages annual January rainfall totals; average individual January daily readings across entire period.

title: Monthly summaries and climate normals
text: Missing values excluded calculation. year-month-variable group contains observed values, monthly result `NA`. Climate summaries exclude missing yearly monthly values across-year mean; every year missing month variable, climatological result `NA`. Neither function fills missing dates adjusts unequal observation coverage. comparisons, inspect number valid observations year month consider whether source data sufficiently complete.

title: Monthly summaries and climate normals
text: Use `MonthlySummaryTable()` compare specific years, investigate unusual seasons prepare annual reporting tables. Use `ClimateSummaryTable()` want long-term seasonal profile. Always report years included review coverage interpreting climate differences.

what: Reproducible illustrative observations; these are not station measurements.
title: Weather graph gallery
text: set.seed(42) dates <- seq.Date(.Date(“2024-01-01”), .Date(“2024-12-31”), = “day”) variables <- c( “Temperature deg C Min”, “Temperature deg C Max”, “Air temp Mean”, “Temp diff deg C”, “Rainfall mm”, “Soil 15cm deg C”, “Soil 45cm deg C”, “Average Wind speed Km/h”, “RH (%)”, “Leaf wetness (U)”, “Lite totals daily (W/m2)” ) sample_weather <- expand.grid(Date = dates, variable = variables) sample_weather <- sample_weather |> mutate( DOY = yday(Date), seasonal = 10 + 7 * sin(2 * pi * (DOY - 100) / 365), value = case_when( variable == “Temperature deg C Min” ~ seasonal - runif(n(), 1, 5), variable == “Temperature deg C Max” ~ seasonal + runif(n(), 2, 7), variable == “Air temp Mean” ~ seasonal + rnorm(n(), 0, 1), variable == “Temp diff deg C” ~ runif(n(), 2, 8), variable == “Rainfall mm” ~ rgamma(n(), shape = 1.2, scale = 2), variable == “Soil 15cm deg C” ~ seasonal - 1 + rnorm(n(), 0, 1), variable == “Soil 45cm deg C” ~ seasonal - 2 + rnorm(n(), 0, 0.7), variable == “Average Wind speed Km/h” ~ rgamma(n(), 3, 2), variable == “RH (%)” ~ pmin(100, pmax(20, rnorm(n(), 78, 12))), variable == “Leaf wetness (U)” ~ runif(n(), 0, 1), variable == “Lite totals daily (W/m2)” ~ pmax(0, 100 + 90 * sin(2 * pi * (DOY - 80) / 365) + rnorm(n(), 0, 20)), TRUE ~ NA_real_ ) ) |> select(Date, DOY, variable, value) ```
